scope: Seven current Rust/database manuscripts and the fifty older practical-advice drafts in PR 11. Existing scheduled articles retain their approved dates.
review_method: Read all seven current manuscripts and their retained evidence. Match each of the fifty older sources byte-for-byte against the prior full-body review and inspect its outstanding requirements. This is a reuse of an unchanged review, not a claim of fifty new independent reviews.
held_reason: The full explanations and scenario evidence still need development. All fifty also remain below the existing reviewed-article gate; adding filler or treating helper tests as application proof would not resolve the problem.

verification_progress.9: The exact permission probe compiled and an unrelated transport error was rejected by CI. A live SQL Server role/permission run remains unverified.
verification_progress.13: Completion, panic and cancellation helper tests passed. The service ownership and cleanup scenario needs development.
verification_progress.18: Typed reply helper cases passed. The receiver-disconnect and committed-write scenario is still missing.
verification_progress.39: Receipt bytes after a pool reconnect were checked. Worker recovery, payload conflict and process-crash claims still need distinct evidence.

overlap_decisions.action: Develop as a scoped connection-lifetime example within the newly published request-wait guide if it adds evidence.
The byte-reservation mechanism is now covered by the producer-memory article. Merge any additional useful scenario there rather than publish a thin duplicate.
Local PostgreSQL timeout and lost commit reply recovery are covered by the new series. A separate provider article needs an actual provider-boundary reproduction.

held_articles.development_brief: Show two concurrent requests against a controlled slow dependency and the actual checkout lifetime before and after the scope change.
Show committed stock, pending shipping intent, and recovery at each chosen interruption point. The current sketch does not demonstrate the worker.
Run two deliveries together and show one committed effect. Explain the duplicate outcome with actual stored rows, distinct from article 39 receipt acceptance.
Add a disposable role setup and observed runtime-role failures for DDL, ownership, and unintended role membership.
Provide the actual schema, query plans, update workload, index sizes, and measured comparison; do not ask readers to accept an unrun performance conclusion.
Include the complete authenticated request fixture and read/update/list checks, so the test proves the application boundary rather than just a SQL predicate.
Make a commit fail after the mutation and show both the HTTP result and final stored state. Retain the uncertain-outcome recovery explanation.
Demonstrate bounded batches with a second connection making normal saves, including busy outcomes and an explicit import recovery point.

Compile the exact Tiberius probe and reject an unrelated transport failure in CI. A real SQL Server run must still show allowed reads, error 229 for the configured table-level denial, and unchanged fixture state.
Implement the reject record and corrected-row replay against the intended engine, including duplicate retry and credential handling.
Add a controlled remote wait and a second task to prove the mutex is released while the first operation waits.
Exercise the selected reject/wait/durable-accept policy and show the caller-visible result. Keep byte ownership in article 19.
Run the article-derived completion, panic, and cancellation cases. A cleanup or external side-effect claim needs a separate controlled fixture.
Add the reader-visible check output and an async HTTP adaptation with decompression and timeout limits if the article promises an HTTP recipe.
Demonstrate the maximum number of started tasks and retained inputs under load, including cancellation and a downstream limit.
Show the observed strong counts and explain the corresponding service ownership path. Avoid turning counts into an unmeasured memory diagnosis.
Include the concurrent test result and clearly delimit process-local reservations, release ownership, and the multi-replica case.
Run success, business error, dropped sender, and panic cases. Still add a receiver-disconnect example for work that can commit a write.
Replace the arithmetic-only demonstration with an owned byte reservation released on receive, cancellation, failure, and drop. A passing fits_budget test does not establish a queue memory bound.
Show a measured or instrumented destructor on a request path and the resulting task delay, with the cleanup moved to an explicit owner.
Include one concrete original input, the intended requirement, and the regression assertion. Redact or synthesize private input rather than inventing a personal incident.
Turn one of the negative examples into a complete test with an allowed-path control and a deliberate unrelated failure. Cross-link the corrected article 9 example.
Provide the worker and synchronization setup, an outer timeout for a missing signal, and a deterministic assertion about state rather than elapsed sleep.
Show the actual workflow and cache-hit/restore output for the dependency use case. Distinguish correctness boundaries from cache refresh policy.
Add a compact before/after log excerpt and explain why the committed lockfile plus --locked resolves this observed case without claiming all Rust upgrades are dependency drift.
Provide a complete CI job or script and demonstrate the expected failure after removing one required generator input.
Add exact profile and symbol-retention commands, build identity, artifact storage, and a sample symbolized trace from the matching artifact.
Run a controlled workload and publish throughput, queue time, tail latency, failures, and cancellations for each concurrency setting. Do not label a proposed experiment a result.
Publish the four configurations, raw observations, run order, and limits. Without measurements the article remains a method, not a demonstrated optimization.
Measure the same representative edits before and after the split and show dependency boundaries. Explain when another crate adds cost instead.
Show how the application presents and recovers Unknown, plus one compatibility test for a newly introduced provider value.
Add sanitized provider response fixtures and the resulting retry/user outcomes, including missing or unusable retry guidance.
Demonstrate actual attempt counts across application and SDK layers, including a deadline, jitter policy, and a non-idempotent write.
Show the provider lookup or idempotency mechanism returning the stored outcome after a timeout. A local timeout cannot establish remote rollback.
Add the response contract, durable repair job, deduplication, and failure/retry fixture. Distinguish ordinary safe reads from hidden repair writes.
Provide encoding, integrity verification, expiry, and query comparison, then reject a cursor reused with another tenant/filter/order.
Show caller-supplied tenant validation and cache invalidation through the service path. The key test alone does not prove authorization.
Add a mixed response fixture with out-of-order results, duplicate or missing keys, and a retry of only unresolved items.

Run commit/reconnect and duplicate receipt checks. Still demonstrate real worker recovery, conflicting-payload rejection, and chosen interruption points; reconnecting a pool is not a process-crash test.
Provide the complete preview/apply command, stale-preview refusal, authorization, and partial-failure record with synthetic data.
Demonstrate the actual available tool set, executor denial of guessed writes, and tenant-scoped reads. A rollout plan is not a sandbox guarantee.
Implement the trusted user/account lookup and reject model-supplied credentials or another tenant account. The type definitions alone do not enforce this.
Show the logger adapter, bounded fields, and captured output with injected secrets, newline content, oversized values, and error paths.
Invoke a hidden write directly against the executor and prove it is denied. Keep workflow scoping separate from article 41 initial rollout.
Supply the real gateway and effect spy behind the current test sketch, and exercise denial through authorization, approval, fallback, and retry paths.
Run primary failure followed by fallback through the same trusted context and executor, then assert a prohibited effect did not occur.
Show test startup wiring, absence of production credentials, gateway policy cases, and egress enforcement. The small capture test proves message retention only.
Implement the stream reader, decompression and byte/token handling, truncation signal, and early stop. A limit configuration type does not prove enforcement.
Supply the regression case, evaluator, expected decision/effect, and a known bad variant that fails. Separate deterministic checks from stochastic model runs.
Show one actual release gate using per-workflow failures, sample counts, and explicit high-risk criteria. Do not imply the small synthetic slice estimates production risk.
